searchText: hey all, etherscan wants to show the % size of a block compared to its target - eg showing 200% when gas limit is 15,000,000 and gas used is 30,000,000 like we currently do here will the gaslimit returned by eth_getblock be the canonical 'target' of a given block under 1559 that we can simply use? or will doing that be circular reasoning Gas limit is 30M in that example. Gas target is half that. ok so **gasLimit** from eth_getblock will be the amount actually used within the block. is there any way we can tell that it is 200/150/100/50% of the current target? is that by looking at trend from previous blocks? and if so what will **gasUsed** represent? `gasLimit` is the gas limit for the block. `gasUsed` is how much gas was actually used in the block. If `gasUsed > gasLimit`, the block is invalid. `gasTarget = gasLimit / 2`. Any chance you might know if there is a jsonrpc field in the pipeline differentiating between gaslimit and gastarget, or would it be good enough to take the current gasLimit response * 2? (i.e. then we will show GasLimit: 30M and GasTarget: 15M for the above example) `gasLimit / 2` is the `gasTarget` as of London. Prior to London, there is no such thing as a `gasTarget`. thanks <@!301186049323958275>! hey, been having a hard time finding good examples of eip-1559 transactions on ropsten, anyone have a few handy? looks like everything I am finding is still legacy just found one digging around this discord https://ropsten.etherscan.io/tx/0x2185827098ea1312af76d63f434348e9f36afaa4090b37abc9594af9d5486e0d any others or an easy way to find some more? yeah sure I did and there are no 1559 txs in them 🙂 instead of spending hours clicking through blocks hoping to find one was hoping someone might have an idea of a few examples, it is a totally new transaction type and people do want to look at them and test them without having to hunt them down on their own, thanks! https://ropsten.etherscan.io/tx/0x2185827098ea1312af76d63f434348e9f36afaa4090b37abc9594af9d5486e0d Does anyone have info about how geth sorts transactions (by default) when 1559 is activated? I'm trying to understand if sorting by `maxPriorityFeePerGas` is a sensible thing to do in Hardhat. <@!453707755765760021> in the block or tx pool? within a block generally sorted by `effectiveMinerFee` so `min(tx.tip, feeCap - baseFee)` ah, makes sense, thanks Does this mean that geth sort its mempool after each block? Because the `baseFee` changes Miners have always resorted the includible transactions each block. After 1559, non-mining nodes will also now sort a fixed portion of their pending txs. Check out the write up linked in the PR for more info: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22898 great! thank you looks like RPC impls currently deviate slightly from the spec - this PR would bring the spec in alignment: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/221 tbh, i'm weakly against the change though

excerpts.author: harithk
excerpts.content:
hey all, 

etherscan wants to show the % size of a block compared to its target - eg showing 200% when gas limit is 15,000,000 and gas used is 30,000,000 like we currently do here

will the gaslimit returned by eth_getblock be the canonical 'target' of a given block under 1559 that we can simply use?

excerpts.author: harithk
excerpts.content: or will doing that be circular reasoning

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Gas limit is 30M in that example.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Gas target is half that.

excerpts.author: harithk
excerpts.content:
ok so **gasLimit** from eth_getblock will be the amount actually used within the block. is there any way we can tell that it is 200/150/100/50% of the current target? is that by looking at trend from previous blocks?

and if so what will **gasUsed** represent?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `gasLimit` is the gas limit for the block.  `gasUsed` is how much gas was actually used in the block.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If `gasUsed > gasLimit`, the block is invalid.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `gasTarget = gasLimit / 2`.

excerpts.author: enigmatic331
excerpts.content:
Any chance you might know if there is a jsonrpc field in the pipeline differentiating between gaslimit and gastarget, or would it be good enough to take the current gasLimit response * 2?

(i.e. then we will show GasLimit: 30M and GasTarget: 15M for the above example)

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `gasLimit / 2` is the `gasTarget` as of London.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Prior to London, there is no such thing as a `gasTarget`.

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content:
Does anyone have info about how geth sorts transactions (by default) when 1559 is activated? 

I'm trying to understand if sorting by `maxPriorityFeePerGas` is a sensible thing to do in Hardhat.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: <@!453707755765760021> in the block or tx pool?

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content: within a block

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: generally sorted by `effectiveMinerFee`

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: so `min(tx.tip, feeCap - baseFee)`

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content: ah, makes sense, thanks

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content: Does this mean that geth sort its mempool after each block? Because the `baseFee` changes

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: Miners have always resorted the includible transactions each block. After 1559, non-mining nodes will also now sort a fixed portion of their pending txs. Check out the write up linked in the PR for more info: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22898

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content: great! thank you

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: looks like RPC impls currently deviate slightly from the spec - this PR would bring the spec in alignment: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/221

excerpts.content: tbh, i'm weakly against the change though
